column1: # RELEASE-BINARY dispositions — scripts/census_release_binaries.py
# One row per binary target the workspace builds:
#     <name><TAB><disposition><TAB><reason>
# `release` = the manifest names it, so `rb-release-manifest verify` covers it.
# `tool`    = built by `cargo build --bins`, deliberately NOT distributed.
# ⛔ THE LEDGER IS THE ONLY LIST. `make release` derives its `--bin` flags from
# the `release` rows here, and the census refuses any binary target this file
# does not cover. Before `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.6.8.1` the Makefile carried a hardcoded
# four while the workspace built ten, and nothing could notice: the six it
# omitted were built into the same directory and named by no manifest.
# ⛔ A DISPOSITION IS A DECISION, SO EVERY ROW CARRIES ITS REASON. ADR-027 makes
# the manifest "the single verification unit" — "binaries verify THROUGH it,
# never individually" — so `tool` is a claim that something is not part of the
# release, not a note that nobody got round to it.
# ⚠️ Adding a binary to the workspace fails the gate until it is adjudicated
# here, in either direction. That is the point: the next one is a decision
# rather than an omission.
rb
column3: the operator CLI — the command a person runs against a deployment

column1: rb-server
column3: the control plane — the deployment's own process

column1: rb-node
column3: the node worker — the process that supervises adapters on a host

column1: rb-journal
column3: ships beside rb-node: the journal inspector IS the recovery path when a node is lost, so a deployment that has rb-node and not this one cannot execute its own runbook

column1: rb-site
column3: the site-operator tool — it performs site-wide acts against a live deployment and verifies storage locality from within the checkout

column1: rb-mcp
column3: the MCP server an MCP client spawns; it is the surface SIGNOFF-REPAIR.6.8 made reachable, and a client executes it directly

column1: reasonbraid-browse
column3: the R3 acquisition worker, and the sharpest case in this file: extraction::worker_path resolves it from current_exe().parent(), so rb-server SPAWNS IT FROM THE RELEASE DIRECTORY ITSELF. An executable sitting there that the manifest does not name is a code-execution path the ADR-027 ladder cannot verify

column1: reasonbraid-extract
column3: the R2 acquisition worker — the same resolution, the same argument

column1: rb-bench
column3: the WP7 deliberation benchmark runner. It produces measurements for a report; nothing in a deployment executes it, and it is not part of what an operator installs

column1: rb-release-manifest
column3: the signer itself, and the reason is circularity rather than convenience: a manifest cannot meaningfully verify the tool that produced it, because checking that entry would require trusting the binary under examination. It is a build-host tool and is verified by being built from this source

column1: rb-reconciler
column3: the §15.8 publication reconciler — a deployment runs it against its own database and publication root to recover interrupted publishes (ROADMAP §7.2's reasonbraid-reconciler)
